bugs.title: Short help stops at an abbreviation inside the first sentence
style() drops color index 0 and accepts invalid colors
bugs.report:
`click.style("x y", fg=0)` returns `x y\x1b[0m` with no color code, but 0 is black in the 256-color palette; `fg=91` correctly gives `\x1b[38;5;91m`. `bg=0` and `click.secho(..., fg=0)` have the same problem.

Invalid colors are also accepted silently: `fg=256`, `fg=0.0`, `fg=()`, `fg=(0, 0)`, `fg=(0, 256, 0)` or `fg=("0", "0", "0")` produce broken escape codes instead of failing. They should raise `ValueError` with a message starting `Unknown color`.

bugs.title: Deprecated label gets a stray leading space when help is empty
bugs.report:
A deprecated command or option with no help text renders its deprecation label with an extra leading space.

```python
@click.command(deprecated=True)
def cli():
    pass
```

`cli --help` prints `   (DEPRECATED)` (three spaces) where every other line is indented by two. For `click.Option(["--foo"], deprecated="USE B INSTEAD")` with no help, the help column reads ` (DEPRECATED: USE B INSTEAD)` with a leading space. Both happen whether the help is `""` or missing.

bugs.title: Usage line is blank when a program has no arguments
bugs.report:
Writing a usage line for a program with no arguments produces only a blank line.

```python
formatter = click.HelpFormatter()
formatter.write_usage("Program")
print(repr(formatter.getvalue()))
```

This prints `'\n'` instead of `'Usage: Program\n'`. A custom prefix is lost the same way (`prefix="Run: "` should give `Run: Program`), and the current indentation should be kept. The line should end at the program name, with no trailing space.

bugs.title: Hidden prompts hide custom validation messages
bugs.report:
When a prompt hides its input, my type's validation message is replaced by a generic one.

```python
class Password(click.ParamType):
    name = "password"
    def convert(self, value, param, ctx):
        if len(value) < 4:
            self.fail("Password must be at least 4 characters", param, ctx)
        return value

click.prompt("Password", hide_input=True, type=Password())
```

Typing `abc` shows `Error: The value you entered was invalid.` instead of `Error: Password must be at least 4 characters`. Without `hide_input` the real message appears. The typed value must still never be revealed: for built-in types the message should mask it (`'***' is not a valid integer`), and a custom message that contains the typed text should fall back to the generic message.

bugs.title: version_option fails when the import name differs from the distribution name
bugs.report:
`@click.version_option(package_name="PIL")` makes `--version` raise `RuntimeError: 'PIL' is not installed`, even though Pillow (which provides the `PIL` module) is installed. The same happens when the package name is detected automatically, and for other packages whose module name differs from their distribution, such as `jwt` from PyJWT.

It should find the distribution that provides that top-level module and print its version. If a module name is provided by more than one installed distribution, the error should say it maps to multiple installed distributions and name them. A name that matches nothing should still say it is not installed.
